A.summary: Broad supply trunks and two-sided regulator copper are strengths. The saved pours create clearance and mask failures, and four copper DRC errors remain after refill.

B.summary: A continuous rear ground fill and 134 ground vias support a fully connected board. The regulator has little local heat-spreading copper, seven vias are inside solderable lands, and the USB B7 branch spends 5.05 mm on the back.

C.summary: C is the preferred order candidate, with complete connectivity, two-sided regulator copper and the best-coupled USB receiver pair. The main electrical weakness is the interrupted ground reference under the main oscillator and long header routes.

D.summary: D has 88 missing connections after refill, including 29 on +5V and 35 on GND. Its matched USB receiver traces cannot compensate for open MCU supplies, oscillator returns and header signals.

human_guess.why: The shaped power pours, offset thermal vias, broad shield return and selective neck-downs suggest hand tuning over several passes. The long SPI-clock detour and tiny leftover SCL segment also fit a locally revised layout.
